paper.title: Achieving Counterfactual Fairness for Causal Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual causal bandit with d-separation set (D-UCB setting)
unmapped: Known causal graph (Markovian SCM) over user features X, arm features A, intermediate variables I and reward R
Known conditional distributions P(z | x_{t,a}) of the d-separation set given user/arm features
Learner observes the realised value of the d-separation set W at each round
Discrete variables; arm selection modelled as a soft intervention (deterministic policies)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\W\subseteq \A\cup\X\cup\mathbf{I}$ be a subset of nodes that d-separates reward $R$ from features $(\A\cup\X) \backslash \W$ in the causal graph. ... we assume that distribution $P(\mathbf{z}| \x_{t,a})$ is known based on previous knowledge that was used to build the causal graph.

settings.name_in_paper: Fair causal bandit with counterfactual fairness constraint (F-UCB setting)
unmapped: Known causal graph and known conditional distributions P(z | x_{t,a})
Counterfactual fairness constraint |Delta_pi| <= tau per round on the policy, with sensitive attribute S
Existence of a known safe policy pi_0 with fairness discrepancy Delta_pi0 < tau at every round (Assumption 3); learner uses tau and Delta_pi0
Fairness-discrepancy error terms are 1-sub-Gaussian and its mean is in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: min \mathcal{R}_T = \sum_{t=1}^{T} ( \mathbb{E}_{\sa \sim \pi_t^*}[\mu_{a}] - \mathbb{E}_{\sa \sim \pi_t}[\mu_{a}] ) s.t. \forall t, \pi_t\in \bar{\Phi}_t ... There exists a safe policy $\pi_0$, i.e., $\pi_0 \in \Pi_t$ such that $\Delta_{\pi_0} \leq \tau$ for each $t \in [T]$.

symbols.W_dom: domain size |W| of the d-separation set W (number of joint values)

conditions: error terms of the reward are 1-sub-Gaussian (Assumption 1)
known causal graph and known P(z|x_{t,a})
holds with probability at least 1 - 2*delta*T*|W| - exp(-|W| log^3(T)/(32 log(1/delta)))

source.label: thm:rb
source.quote: Given a causal graph $\mathcal{G}$, with probability at least $1-2\delta T |\mathbf{W}| - \exp(- \frac{|\mathbf{W}| \log^3(T)}{32\log(1/\delta)})$, the regret of D-UCB is bounded by \[ \mathcal{R}_T \leq \sqrt{|\mathbf{W}| T\log(T)}log(T) + \sqrt{32|\mathbf{W}|T \log(1/\delta)} \] where $|\mathbf{W}|$ is the domain space of set $\W$.

results.notes: Regret defined as sum_t (mu_{a*} - mu_{a_t}) via means, high probability. Algorithm does not take T as input, but the failure probability depends on T; horizon labelled anytime with some uncertainty.

symbols.W_dom: domain size |W| of the d-separation set W

conditions: holds with probability at least 1 - 2|W|/T - exp(-|W| log^2(T)/64)

source.quote: By setting $\delta = 1/T^2$, the causal bandit algorithm achieves $\Tilde{O}(\sqrt{|\mathbf{W}| \cdot T})$ regret bound.

results.notes: Statement gives O_tilde(sqrt(|W| T)); the proof gives the explicit 16*sqrt(|W| T log T) log T bound, recorded here. Equivalent to O_tilde(sqrt(W_dom*T)).

symbols.W_dom: domain size |W| of the d-separation set W
symbols.Delta_pi0: maximum fairness discrepancy of the safe policy pi_0 across rounds

conditions: 1-sub-Gaussian errors for reward and fairness discrepancy; means in [0,1] (Assumptions 1-2)
existence of safe policy pi_0 with Delta_pi0 <= tau every round (Assumption 3)
holds with probability at least 1 - delta_E

source.label: cfbound
source.quote: Given a causal graph $\mathcal{G}$, let $\delta_E = 4|\mathbf{W}|T\delta$ and $\Delta_{\pi_0}$ denote the maximum fairness discrepancy of a safe policy $\pi_0$ across all rounds. Setting $\alpha_c = 1$ and $\alpha_r = \frac{2}{\tau - \Delta_{\pi_0}}$, with probability at least $1-\delta_E$, the cumulative regret of F-UCB is bounded by: \[ \mathcal{R}_T \leq (\frac{2}{\tau - \Delta_{\pi_0}}+1) \times ( 2\sqrt{2T|\mathbf{W}|\log(1/\delta_E)} + 4\sqrt{T\log(2/\delta_E)\log(1/\delta_E)} ) \]

results.notes: With delta_E = 1/T^2 the paper claims O_tilde(sqrt(|W|T)/(tau - Delta_pi0)). Proof's internal logs use log(1/delta) rather than log(1/delta_E); recorded as stated. Regret is against the unconstrained optimal policy per round.
